correctness.rationale: Exact conditional ordered-prefix/sorted-tail coupling from [Clay 2026] keeps the descent and inversion statistics on the same uniforms. The inversion Hoeffding projection has coefficients n-2t+1 on t<=k and -k afterwards; orthogonal canonical kernels give remainder variance k(2n-k-1)/24=O(n²). Prefix-descent covariance with the inversion projection equals (k-1)/6, negligible at sqrt(n) by n^(3/2) joint scaling. Bounded 1-dependent triangular-array blocking gives independent conditional Gaussian order noise. Occupancy count obeys its classical CLT and independently perturbs the means by slopes 1/2 and (1-a)/2. Mean-square random-index bounds complete the joint CLT. The actual package verifier independently checks 202 exact finite algebra and coupling cases; finite checks are not invoked as asymptotic proofs.

originality.rationale: The primary March 2026 full-text paper states separate descent and inversion CLTs but no bivariate limit or intermediate-time cross-covariance. The full uniform-permutation joint-extremes paper treats a distinct fully randomized measure and does not imply the intermediate move-to-top positive covariance. The riffle-shuffle paper refers to a different transition kernel. Searches were evaluated by statement implication, not just matching titles; previous published related comparisons do not dominate this claim. Older or differently named joint Markov-chain shuffle CLTs pose a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The interaction between two canonical card-shuffle observables cannot be inferred from the two known marginal Gaussian laws. The identified strictly positive finite-c covariance is quantitatively controlled by fluctuations in coupon occupancy even though order noise is asymptotically independent. The result gives a precise joint law and an occupancy-canceling linear combination, mathematically natural for separating mixing diagnostics; not a routine restatement of known univariate variance formulas.
